text:
A three-year-old boy who had a medical emergency at a nursery near Manchester died from choking on food, an inquest has heard.
Thiago Wall was taken to hospital from Cosy Toes nursery in Middleton on 2 November, a week after his third birthday.
A hearing at Rochdale coroner’s court on Wednesday was told that Thiago died three days later and the provisional cause of death was “choking on a bowl of food”.
Greater Manchester police (GMP) are investigating the circumstances of the tragedy in line with usual procedure after a death in a care setting.
The force confirmed on Wednesday that no arrests had been made and inquiries were ongoing.
Joanne Kearsley, the senior coroner, said Thiago was at the nursery on 2 November when there was an “incident there in which he was found to be choking”.
Kearsley said a CT scan found the boy had suffered “an unsurvivable hypoxic brain injury”.
The court heard that the GMP investigation would “take months rather than weeks” and no date was set for a full inquest.
Kearsley said: “I am sure everybody would wish to express our condolences to Thiago’s family.”
Cosy Toes Nursery Ltd was suspended by the regulator Ofsted from operating its four nurseries in Middleton on 5 November, the day Thiago died.
In a statement last week, the nurseries firm said: “We are all heartbroken to hear the tragic news of Thiago’s passing. He was a wonderful and beautiful child, and our thoughts and prayers are all with his family at this terrible time.
“We will of course give our fullest possible assistance in every way possible to the inquiries that must rightly follow this tragic event.”
Its suspension by Ofsted means the nurseries cannot operate for six weeks, due to concerns of a risk to child safety. The regulator can lift the suspension after six weeks or extend it to 12 weeks or longer.
Ofsted said last week it was assisting the police investigation and added: “Our thoughts are with the family of the young boy and everyone affected by this deeply distressing incident.”
